name: Lisbon Botanical Garden (Jardim Botânico de Lisboa)
seoTitle: Lisbon Botanical Garden: A Shady Hour in Príncipe Real
tagline: A 19th-century university garden on a steep hillside in Príncipe Real; the upper terrace is free, the lower arboretum costs €5

description.short: The University of Lisbon's botanical garden, planted from 1873 on the slopes below Príncipe Real and classified as a National Monument in 2010. The upper 'Classe' is free; the lower 'Arboreto' needs a ticket (€5 adults).
description.full:
The Jardim Botânico is a good choice for a quieter hour on a hot day, or for anyone interested in plants, but it is not a priority on a first, short call. It sits about 3.4 km from the terminal on the hill of Príncipe Real, so take a taxi (about 10 to 12 minutes) to the entrance at Rua da Escola Politécnica 58, next to the Museu Nacional de História Natural e da Ciência. Tram 24 and buses 758 and 773 also stop outside.

The garden has two levels. The upper terrace, the Classe, is free during opening hours and has benches, palms and views over the trees below; if you only have 20 minutes, see this. The lower Arboreto, reached by steep paths and steps, needs a ticket and is where the large trees, palms, cycads and ponds are. Allow an hour for both. The former butterfly house has been replaced by a sensory garden, the Jardim dos Sentidos.

From October to March the garden opens 10:00 to 17:00; from April to September, 09:00 to 20:00, with last entry 30 minutes before closing. It closes only on 25 December and 1 January. Entry is free for everyone on Sundays from 10:00 to 13:00, which is also when local families come.

The garden is left deliberately natural: fallen leaves and dry undergrowth are kept as habitat, and in summer only the essentials are watered, so it can look parched from July to September. Spring is when it looks its best.

It pairs well with a downhill walk back towards the ship: through the Jardim do Príncipe Real, past the São Pedro de Alcântara viewpoint, down through Bairro Alto and Chiado to the Baixa, then east along the river. The Glória funicular next to the viewpoint is closed, so walk down Calçada da Glória or the side streets. From the garden to the terminal on foot is about 50 minutes, mostly downhill.
description.history: The site on the Monte Olivete hill had been used for teaching botany since the Jesuit college of Cotovia stood here from 1609 to 1759. A plan for a scientific garden attached to the Escola Politécnica was drawn up in 1843, but planting only began in 1873, led by the professors Conde de Ficalho and Andrade Corvo. The German gardener Edmund Goeze laid out the upper Classe and the Frenchman Jules Daveau the lower Arboreto, with plants gathered from Portuguese territories worldwide. The first seed catalogue appeared in 1878. In the late 1930s and early 1940s, director Ruy Telles Palhinha regrouped the upper beds by ecology, and the city restored the garden in 2016.
description.significance: It is one of Portugal's main historic scientific gardens and was classified as a National Monument in 2010. Its collections of palms and cycads, and of species from New Zealand, Australia, China, Japan and South America, show how mild Lisbon's climate is. For a visitor it offers shade and quiet in the centre of the city, and the top terrace costs nothing.

directions.general: Located in Príncipe Real district between Rato and Jardim do Príncipe Real, near São Pedro de Alcântara viewpoint
directions.fromCruisePort: About 3.4 km and 50 minutes on foot with steep hills, so take a taxi (about 12 minutes) to the Príncipe Real entrance, or the metro to Rato and walk 8 minutes downhill.
directions.publicTransport: Metro: Rato station (Yellow line) - 6-minute walk. Tram 28 stops nearby. Tram 24 or Bus 758 stop at Praça do Príncipe Real entrance. Multiple bus routes serve the area.
directions.parking: Limited street parking in Príncipe Real. Public parking at Rato metro station nearby.

distanceFromCruisePort.walkingTime: Not practical on foot (51 min walk)

openingTimes.currentStatus: Open daily except 25 December and 1 January

admissionPrices.notes: 2026 prices for the garden (lower Arboreto): adults €5; seniors 65+ €4; students €2.50; family (2 adults + children up to 17) €12.50; children 2-10 free. Museum + garden €8 adults. The upper Classe is free at all times, and the whole garden is free on Sundays 10:00-13:00. Lisboa Card: 10% off.

visitingInformation.averageVisitDuration: 20 minutes for the free upper terrace; about 1 hour for the whole garden
visitingInformation.bestTimeToVisit: Weekday mornings, and spring for the garden at its greenest. Sunday mornings are free but busier.
visitingInformation.adviceForVisitors: Wear shoes with grip for the steep lower paths. Bring water in summer. Fallen leaves and dry patches are deliberate, not neglect. Combine with Príncipe Real and the São Pedro de Alcântara viewpoint.

cruisePassengerInfo.timeNeededFromPort: About 2-2.5 hours: taxi up, an hour in the garden, then about 50 minutes' walk downhill back to the ship
cruisePassengerInfo.accessibility: Taxi about 10-12 minutes to Rua da Escola Politécnica 58; tram 24 and buses 758 and 773 stop outside. The lower garden is steep.
combinableWith: Miradouro de São Pedro de Alcântara
Museu Nacional de História Natural e da Ciência
tips: Take a taxi up and walk back down: the garden is on a hill, and the return to the ship is mostly downhill.
The upper 'Classe' terrace is free during opening hours; pay €5 only if you want the steep lower 'Arboreto'.
Everyone gets in free on Sundays from 10:00 to 13:00.
Children aged 2 to 10 are free, and seniors 65+ pay €4.
The butterfly house mentioned in older guides has gone; it is now a sensory garden.
In summer the garden is only watered where necessary, so expect dry patches from July to September.
The Glória funicular by the São Pedro de Alcântara viewpoint is closed; walk down to the Baixa instead.
Winter closing is 17:00 with last entry at 16:30, so do not leave it to the end of the day from October to March.

highlights: Upper 'Classe' terrace, free during opening hours
Lower 'Arboreto' with large trees, ponds and cascades (ticketed)
Cycad collection, one of the garden's best-known features
Species from New Zealand, Australia, China, Japan and South America
Jardim dos Sentidos, a sensory garden that replaced the butterfly house
facilities: Ticket office shared with the Museu Nacional de História Natural e da Ciência
Two wheelchairs and portable ramps on request at the ticket office
Audio trails (itinerários sonoros) on the museum website
Museum next door (separate or combined ticket)

accessibility.mobilityNotes: The upper Classe is the easier part. The lower Arboreto is on a steep slope with stairs and uneven paths that are hard for wheelchairs and anyone unsteady on their feet. Two wheelchairs are available on request at the ticket office.
